thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: runtime crashloop detected on cluster/gpu-pool-us-east-3 (sev=page)

incident-bot: Alert rule 'runtime.container.restarts > 5m' fired for service=redwood-runtime, node=ip-10-48-13-22, pod=runtime-llm-0.

anya: I'm on it — pinging oncall. Looks like repeated segfaults in the engine process.

sam_oncall: I'm up, grabbing logs. Any customer reports?

elaine_pm: Two customers reported increased 5xx and tail latency spikes ~10:12 UTC. One is a priority enterprise tenant.

mike_infra: Docker logs show SIGSEGV in /opt/runtime/bin/engine at startup, then container restarts. Kernel OOMs not obvious yet. Posting excerpt: 

```
[2026-03-15T10:13:04Z] runtime[1]: runtime: failed to allocate kv cache buffer
[2026-03-15T10:13:04Z] runtime[1]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f3a2b4c4f20 sp 0x7ffda7c4e7a0 error 4 in libengine.so[7f3a2b400000+1a0000]
[2026-03-15T10:13:04Z] kernel: audit: type=1701 audit(1678872784.123:456): auid=1000 uid=1000 gid=1000 ses=2 pid=2345 comm="engine" exe="/opt/runtime/bin/engine" sig=11
```

ops-bot: kubectl describe pod runtime-llm-0 -n prod: Container runtime-llm terminated with signal 11 (Segmentation fault). Restart count: 7.

sam_oncall: Reproduced on host: ip-10-48-13-22. Core file exists at /var/lib/cores/core.engine. Starting gdb quickbacktrace.

mike_infra: Pulling coredump now. If this is a fused kernel path (TensorRT or custom fused op), might be related to a recent quantized kernel rollout. I see recent deploy ID: deploy/2026-03-15-09-58-quant-kernels.

anya: Good catch — can we confirm deploy + crash timing?

sam_oncall: Timeline: deploy finished 09:58, first crash spike 10:12, escalations at 10:14. Matches.

elaine_pm: Customer impact: enterprise-azc saw 27% request errors and queued retries. They're on dedicated capacity but we route fallback traffic through hosted pool when their nodes are short — those fallbacks are tripping.

mike_infra: GDB bt: 

```
#0  0x00007f3a2b4c4f20 in fused_kernel::invoke() at fused.cpp:423
#1  0x00007f3a2b4012e7 in engine::run_inference() at engine.cpp:1290
#2  0x000055aaab123f8c in main_loop() at runtime_main.cpp:88
#3  0x00007f3a29f6a0b3 in __libc_start_main
```

sam_oncall: Looks like fused_kernel::invoke() line, pointer deref inside custom fused op. Possibly NVLink device pointer null after a node flap or GPU reset.

anya: Immediate mitigation options: 1) scale down affected daemonset (remove pod from rotation) 2) cordon node and drain 3) roll back last quant-kernel deploy 4) route affected customer traffic to Dedicated pool. Which is fastest?

mike_infra: Fastest = cordon+drain the node (prevents restarts there), and scale a safe variant (non-fused kernel) of engine as temporary. I can cordon ip-10-48-13-22 now.

sam_oncall: Do it. Also set rollout timeout to prevent automated rollout to other nodes.

ops-bot: kubectl cordon ip-10-48-13-22 -> success.

ops-bot: kubectl drain ip-10-48-13-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -> success (pods evicted).

mike_infra: Node cordoned & drained. I also scaled down runtime pool on that node's AZ and scaled up a fallback pool with env VAR ENGINE_USE_FUSED=0 to prefer non-fused kernels: 

```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runtime-llm ENGINE_USE_FUSED=0 --record
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/runtime-llm
```

sam_oncall: Restarted rollout to non-fused variant. Rolling logs look cleaner so far — new pods start without segfault.

elaine_pm: Notifying impacted customer: we told them we've routed their fallbacks to dedicated capacity and are investigating a kernel regression. They've acknowledged and asked for ETA.

anya: Forensics next: gather full core dump, fused kernel binary + symbol table, and nvcrash logs from the node. I'll open a triage doc and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

mike_infra: I pulled core + libs to staging and reproduced locally. Repro steps involve a long context length request hitting quantized attention path. Failed pointer seems to be from a stale GPU memory handle after an async free.

sam_oncall: Quick fix candidate: a guard in fused_kernel::invoke() to check pointer validity and fall back to CPU path or safe kernel instead of deref. That can be a hotfix if accepted by eng-runtime.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Created patch branch: fix/fused-nullptr-guard and opened PR #4210 (eng-runtime). CI flagged one test flake but compile looks good.

anya: Can we hotpatch into the running image before full rollout? We prefer building a patched image and scoping to canary AZ first.

mike_infra: I'll approve a canary rollout to us-east-3a, keep other AZs on non-fused fallback.

sam_oncall: Monitoring error rate: enterprise-azc errors down from 27% -> 3% after routing. Tail latency also stabilizing. Marking customer impact = partial and mitigated.

elaine_pm: I'll update the customer with the mitigation and ETA for root cause fix (we'll give 24-48h for full fix and patch rollout).

anya: Handing off to oncall-next. @sam_oncall: please include notes for follow-up: collect all traces, PR link, canary rollout plan, and retention location for coredump.

sam_oncall: Handoff done. Notes: coredump at s3://redwood-dumps/3101234567-core.tar.gz; PR #4210; rolled runtime-llm to ENGINE_USE_FUSED=0 across hosted pool; cordoned ip-10-48-13-22 (will remain cordoned until infra confirms hardware/driver health).

incident-bot: Incident update (sev=page -> sev=disruptive): customer impact mitigated, root cause suspected regression in quantized fused kernel.

anya: Thanks team. Assigning eng-runtime to ship PR and eng-ml to audit quant kernel tests. I'll keep the postmortem and timeline in the incident doc.

elaine_pm: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the customer and attach postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
